STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced correctness issue: after a handler calls `WriteHeader(200)` and then hijacks, the held status line and headers are dropped, so the client receives only the raw bytes. Everything else I probed held: ETag computation, If-None-Match parsing, 304 headers, 1xx, non-200 streaming, Compress composition, ServeContent, panics, trailers, and races under `-race`. The probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the start.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files `middleware/zz_probe_test.go` and `middleware/zz_probe2_test.go` were created and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Hijack after a held 200 loses the status line and headers. `w.WriteHeader(200); w.Write("HELLO"); http.NewResponseController(w).Hijack(); rw.WriteString("RAW")`. Plain server output: `"HTTP/1.1 200 OK|Date…|Transfer-Encoding: chunked||RAW"`. With `ETag` outer: `"RAW"`. net/http flushes the header before handing over the conn; this middleware discards it, so the client gets a malformed response. Criterion 10 says Hijack forwards, and the criteria do not carve out this case. Fix: on Hijack with a held 200, flush the snapshot status and headers (and buffered body) first, or document the difference.
- [minor] Content-Type sniffing can differ when a handler writes in several small chunks (`"<"` then `"!DOCTYPE html…"`). Not reproduced on a real server, where both variants sniff `text/html`. Only the recorder showed a difference, and that was a recorder artifact.
- [minor] HEAD via ServeContent gets no ETag while its GET response does. Criterion 3 permits this (the handler wrote no body bytes), but the HEAD and GET responses are inconsistent.
- [minor] A held 200 is fully buffered in memory. This is documented in the doc comment, so no action is needed unless the orchestrator wants a size bound.

CHECKS:
- `ifNoneMatch` table (30 cases: `"a","b"`, `, ,"a"`, `abc`, `"unterminated`, `W/abc`, `""`, whitespace-only, prefix `"ab"` vs `"abc"`, case `"ABC"`, weak both ways, `*` variants, commas inside tags, `"a\"b"`) → pass
- Empty-body GET gets sha256("") ETag → pass
- One Write vs byte-by-byte vs io.Copy(strings.Reader) vs io.Copy(*os.File) → same ETag and body → pass
- HEAD via chi `GetHead`, with ETag outer and with GetHead outer, compared to GET → same ETag, empty body → pass
- HEAD with no body bytes → no ETag → pass
- Handler weak ETag `W/"mine"` matched by `"mine"` → 304 with ETag kept → pass
- 304 headers: Content-Type/Length/Encoding/Last-Modified removed; Cache-Control, Vary, Expires, Content-Location, X-Keep, Date kept; no body → pass
- Non-200 (404) Flush streams before the handler returns (real server) → pass
- Double WriteHeader (404 then 500) → 404 kept, no panic → pass
- Body before WriteHeader(404) → implicit 200 wins → pass
- 103 with Link forwarded; final 200 ETagged → pass
- Hijack/Push errors use the compress.go wording; Unwrap non-nil → pass
- ResponseController.Flush during a buffered 200 → recorder not flushed → pass
- Panic: nothing written, panic propagates; Recoverer outside gives 500 → pass
- Logger outside → pass
- POST with If-None-Match `*` → 200, no ETag, body intact → pass
- Late header and late ETag after write ignored → pass
- Late trailer declared via `Trailer` → delivered → pass
- 100 concurrent requests under `-race` → pass
- (a) `ETag, Compress(5)` real server: gzip decodes correctly, Vary kept, gzip If-None-Match → 304, identity request with gzip ETag → 200, identity and gzip ETags differ → pass
- (b) ETag with GetHead in both orders → pass
- (c) ServeContent: Range → 206, full GET, If-None-Match → 304, HEAD has Content-Length 16; handler-set ETag with ServeContent → 304 → pass
- Hijack after WriteHeader(200) → [blocking] above
- Checklist: README row sits in alphabetical order (after CleanPath, before GetHead), link line after ContentCharset and before GetHead → pass
- Hostile `W/`/quote-only fragments (`W/"`, `""`, `"`) never panic → pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should Hijack after a held 200 flush the snapshot status and headers, or is it acceptable to document that Hijack discards the held response? If the fix is to flush, round 2 should re-run the Hijack probe above.
